desk.headline: HEPS up 4.4% to 254.3c on revenue up 11.8% to R12.1bn; order book a record R39bn; dividend up 8.6% to 88c
results: Revenue rose 11.8% to R12.12bn but operating profit grew only 2.5% to R618m, so margins narrowed.
Headline earnings per share rose 4.4% to 254.3c; the gross interim dividend went up to 88c from 81c.
Materials handling and mining swung to a R111.1m operating loss on weak results at Bauba Resources and higher input costs.
Roads and earthworks revenue rose almost 20% with flat profit; Western Australia swung to a R145.1m profit; infrastructure revenue fell 16%.
The order book climbed 24% to a record R39bn and cash generation more than doubled.

guidance.summary: Raubex gives no figures. It expects renewed tender activity in roads, rail, renewable energy and water to support its pipeline and remains positive on medium- to long-term prospects, though contract awards are still below historical levels.

points: CEO Felicia Msiza said procurement is improving but early FY27 contract awards were still below past levels.
Raubex is trying to sell its whole stake in Bauba Resources to focus on infrastructure; she said there is no certainty a deal will close.
Recent wins include four Sanral road projects worth R1.54bn, preferred bidder on the Limpopo border post and Gautrain civil works.
Uncertainty over South Africa's ferrochrome smelters continues to weigh on bentonite demand.

Conversion of the R39bn order book into revenue and margin recovery.
